§C.5 Ground Truth — Images, Diagrams and Other

Workflow for pages carrying figures: images, logos, diagrams, maps, schematics, floor plans, chemical structures and printed music. The rules themselves live in the protocol; this page only says what to do around them.

  1. Classify the figure before transcribing it. Decide what it really is — text, chart, graph, labelled schematic, photo — and pick the encoding from Images§12.1.1.
  2. Flag every page that falls under an open point, so the page can be revisited when the point closes:
    • a logo that carries no legible text — Logos§12.1.3;
    • a floor plan or architectural drawing — Blueprints§12.2.1;
    • a circuit schematic — Electrical Schematics§12.2.3;
    • a map, and always a data map whose values have no printed key or one that needs both a description and a table — Geographic Maps§12.2.4;
    • a labelled conceptual diagram — Slide Diagrams§12.2.5;
    • a page of printed staves — Music Notation§13.2.
  3. Flag an unreadable part of a chemical structure alongside the words that describe it, so a reviewer can check the source rather than the guess — Chemical Molecules§13.1.
  4. Check an organisation chart's edges against the printed rules, one box at a time; do not add an edge the page does not draw — Diagrams and Flowcharts§12.2.2.
  5. Before publishing a figure page, compare every printed string on the figure with the output — labels, legend entries, scale bars, callouts, captions. A missing string is the most common defect on these pages.
